body:
Source: the ADLC principle-fidelity audit (delta.md, PR #486). Split out of seam 7 during build.

The suppression-marker scan (packages/rails-guard/lib/suppressions.mjs, findSuppressions)
matches via case-sensitive scanText.includes(marker) over the closed list SUPPRESSION_MARKERS,
exported from that same module — read it there for the canonical spellings. This ticket names
each marker DESCRIPTIVELY rather than quoting it, because the rails-guard suppression scan reads
this ticket's own JSON and a literal marker here would flag as a real escape hatch.

The audit flagged the scan as dodgeable by case/whitespace/unicode. BUILDING seam 7 surfaced
that the obvious fix — blanket case/whitespace/unicode normalization — is WRONG and would
DEGRADE the gate:

- The JS skip and only test modifiers, the TypeScript ts-ignore and ts-expect-error directives,
  ESLint's disable comment, pytest's expected-fail marker, and Rust's ignore attribute are all
  CASE-SENSITIVE in their own tools. A mangled/upper-cased or homoglyph variant is INERT — it
  dodges the scanner but also fails to suppress anything. Normalizing them would false-positive
  on non-functional lookalikes and block legitimate code.
- The one genuinely OPERATIVE dodge is flake8's noqa comment. flake8 honors it case-insensitively
  and with any interior whitespace between the hash and the word (none, one space, or several),
  so the no-space form, the all-caps forms, and the extra-space form all really do suppress. The
  current exact-substring test for the single canonical hash-space-lowercase spelling misses
  every one of those operative forms.

So the correct fix is OPERATIVE-AWARE and per-marker, not blanket normalization — the
operative-vs-inert-authoritative lens the doctrine already prescribes for text-scanning gates.

CROSS-MODEL GATED at P5 (touches packages/rails-guard, an enforcement/trust-root package):
a same-model clean prosecute is not enough; needs a cross-model-review approve.

NORMATIVE BEHAVIOR
1. Match the noqa comment case-insensitively and with optional interior whitespace
   (regex /#\s*noqa/i), covering flake8's honored forms, without touching the case-sensitive
   markers.
2. Do NOT case/unicode-normalize the case-sensitive markers; adding false positives on inert
   lookalikes is the bug. If a marker has documented operative variants in its tool, match
   those specifically; otherwise keep the exact-substring match.
3. Preserve the hardened diff parser and the doc/MDX inert-span handling unchanged.

## Acceptance Criteria

- An added line carrying an operative noqa variant the current scan misses — the no-space form, and an all-caps form — is flagged as a suppression. verify: `node --test packages/rails-guard/test/suppressions-operative.test.mjs`
- An added line carrying an INERT upper-cased variant of a case-sensitive marker (an upper-cased skip modifier, an upper-cased ts-ignore directive) is NOT flagged — no false positive. verify: `node --test packages/rails-guard/test/suppressions-operative.test.mjs`
- Existing suppression tests still pass unchanged. verify: `node --test packages/rails-guard/test/suppressions.test.mjs`

allow-suppression: none
title: rails-guard: catch operative suppression-marker dodges (not blanket normalization)
